properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's UCSF campus pass: real OSM building footprint. BLOCK NUMBER ADDED 2026-09-22: cross-checking both OCII's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map and UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation (map updated December 2024) confirmed this building is Block 24C. The project's block_inventory brief had wrongly labeled it '23B' (that number is correctly Third Street Garage) and separately, wrongly, assigned '24C' to a different, unrelated building (Exchange on 16th/1700 Owens St); see docs/briefs/mission_bay_block_inventory.csv for the full correction. Geometry unchanged. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the Block 24C identification is confirmed by UCSF's June 12, 2025 CAC presentation (sfocii.org 2025-06 Item 2, p.3 map, 'MAP UPDATED: DECEMBER 2024'), which labels 'BYERS HALL (24C)' (read directly 2026-09-29); that deck is now in source_doc_urls. The OCII Dec 2019 Land Use Map was reported by the audit reviewers to carry '24A/B' and '24C' labels but tying a label to this footprint there needs a visual check.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.
properties.notes: OCII plan block 24C. Home to QB3 (California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences): Wikipedia says Byers Hall hosts the QB3 director's office and central administration, and a former project manager's portfolio page says it provides space for collaboration between academic researchers and the biotechnology industry. Architect Bohlin Cywinski Jackson (corroborated by a former project manager's own portfolio and an architecture-press article, not confirmed directly on a UCSF-owned page). Opened 2005 (year only; exact month and square footage not found in any source checked).
